title: How Castration Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explore castration across history and today: the warning that this is unlike circumcision, Thomas Jefferson's 1778 bill proposing castration as punishment for rape, polygamy and sodomy, and claims about Genghis Khan and the Chinese admiral Zheng He. They discuss longevity studies of castrated men (a 2012 Korean study), and Boston Corbett, who shot John Wilkes Booth and castrated himself. They cover self-castration as a sign of psychosis, a Bible verse (Matthew 19:12) used by self-castrators, and an internet survey of people who want castration. Korean eunuchs served as trusted court officials, and the Middle Eastern harem guards were eunuchs. The hosts describe 18th-century Italian castrati, the operation before puberty, and the physiology of their voices. Alan Turing's forced hormone treatment is covered, followed by chemical castration in the US (John Money, medroxyprogesterone acetate), California's policy, Joseph Frank Smith, and surgical castration of sex offenders in Germany and the Czech Republic. The episode ends with the ethics debate, consensual castration for sexual gratification in Waynesville, North Carolina (Master Rick Ciarra), and a Heaven's Gate mention. The show closes with listener mail and thank-yous.
topics: Stuff You Should Know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and Jefferson, Genghis Khan notes
segments.summary: Hosts introduce castration as distinct from circumcision, then discuss Thomas Jefferson's castration punishment bill, revisionist views of his relationship with Sally Hemings, and unverified claims about Genghis Khan and Zheng He being castrated.

segments.title: Castration in history and longevity claims
segments.summary: Castrated officials were common in ancient Asia, especially Korea and China. A 2012 Korean study reported longer lifespans and more centenarians among castrated men, with the hosts noting confounding factors such as cushier lives.

segments.title: Boston Corbett and self-castration
segments.summary: Boston Corbett, believed to have shot John Wilkes Booth, castrated himself after being widowed, out of fear of temptation. The hosts discuss the mad hatter mercury theory, which they say is disputed, and a Matthew 19:12 verse cited by Corbett and an early church father.

segments.title: Psychosis and self-castration case study
segments.summary: A 2006 case study described a 20-year-old who castrated himself, with possible Cotard's delusion, and reported relief afterward. The hosts note self-mutilation, not castration itself, is usually labeled psychosis. An internet survey of 112 people gave reasons people want castration.

segments.title: Eunuchs as trusted officials and harem guards
segments.summary: Eunuchs were trusted as court officials in Korea, and in the Middle East they guarded harems because they posed no sexual threat. Korean eunuchs had to adopt sons who were also castrated. The hosts describe a gruesome Korean practice.

segments.title: Italian castrati and castrato singing voices
segments.summary: In 18th-century Italy, castrati sang in churches and opera because women could not. Boys were castrated before puberty by an underground network, and the hosts explain the physiology that preserved a high voice with adult lung and rib growth. The practice was outlawed in Italy in 1870.

segments.title: Alan Turing and early chemical castration
segments.summary: Alan Turing was given a choice between prison and hormone injections (stilbestrol) after being convicted for homosexuality, and died in 1954 after eating a cyanide-laced apple. The hosts note chemical castration spread to the US in the mid-1960s.

segments.title: Chemical and surgical castration of sex offenders
segments.summary: John Money developed a chemical castration regimen using medroxyprogesterone acetate, first voluntary and later compulsory in California. Joseph Frank Smith became a public advocate, then reoffended after stopping injections. Germany and the Czech Republic used surgical castration for sex offenders, and a German study reported low recidivism.

segments.title: Ethics of state castration and voluntary castration for sexual gratification
segments.summary: The hosts summarize arguments against state castration as cruel punishment and as prevention. They then describe the Waynesville, North Carolina case in which Master Rick Ciarra and partners performed unlicensed castrations for consenting clients. Ciarra served a year in prison.

segments.title: Heaven's Gate mention
segments.summary: The hosts note that the male members of Heaven's Gate, including leader Marshall Applewhite, were castrated.

segments.title: Listener mail and thank-you gifts
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners for knives, bracelets, tops, bottle openers, books, postcards, and other gifts, and give contact information.
